policy_note: This corpus checks non-load-bearing panel connection removal and component requalification semantics. It does not calculate tool trajectories, removal forces, structural stability, safety interlocks, material properties, or physical reuse eligibility.

semantics.removal: Requires current panel/as-built/component, sequence, tool and calibration evidence, observed accessible connection, compatible tool, qualified release process, removal force at or below the declared fixture limit, and required support.
semantics.component: Intact/requalified components may proceed. Single-use, damaged, failed-dimension or wear-exceeded components cannot be reused. Repair must pass its own qualified process and independent requalification.
semantics.reassembly: Accepted only after current fastening, torque, geometry and functional evidence; unknown function remains Unknown.
semantics.resource: Shared fixture uses are summed; overbooking blocks the work package.

cases.description: Visible, correctly identified fastener with a calibrated compatible tool and fully passed requalification/reassembly.
Connection is occluded; removal must abstain pending further observation.
The selected tool is incompatible with the declared connection.
As-built connection type differs from the released design.
Stripped fastener head has a separately qualified alternate removal process.
Corrosion/removal force exceeds the declared non-damaging limit.
Adhesive connection lacks a qualified release process.
Connection-sequence evidence is stale.
Removal force exceeds the declared support/stability envelope.
Temporary support is required but its evidence is absent.
Component ID does not match the released bill of materials.
Panel/as-built registration is stale.
Sensor coverage is occluded at the connection required by the work instruction.
Removal damages an adjacent component.
Removed component fails dimensional requalification despite an accepted host panel.
Component condition evidence is unknown.
A designated single-use fastener is incorrectly proposed for reuse.
Recovered component requires a qualified repair before requalification.
A repaired component passes independent requalification and post-reassembly function tests.
Repair fails its independent acceptance check.
Reassembly torque evidence is missing.
Geometry passes but the declared water/air/acoustic function remains untested.
Repeated disassembly cycles exceed the declared wear limit.
Two panel operations overbook the shared fixture resource.
